summary: Iteration 3: validated feature 19 (Import Barang dari Excel) end-to-end. Added /app/backend/tests/test_item_import.py with 8 pytest cases covering template download (owner/kasir), auth guards, invalid file, >5MB rejection, dry-run rules (baru/update/error/duplicate), Indonesian number parsing, header-row auto-detect within first 10 rows, and real import creating item + IMPORT stock movement while leaving stock of existing item untouched. Full regression suite 49/49 pass. Playwright UI test logged in as owner, opened item-import-dialog, uploaded xlsx (1 baru + 1 update + 1 error), verified summary counts (1/1/1), submit label 'Proses Import (2 barang)', result table rendered, after Proses Import dialog closed, success toast shown, new item visible in table, and template download produced template-import-barang.xlsx.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_import._parse reads only the FIRST worksheet (wb.worksheets[0]). If a user accidentally reorders sheets and 'Petunjuk' is first, import will fail with 'Kolom Nama Barang tidak ditemukan'. Consider matching by sheet name 'Barang' first with first-sheet fallback.

routes_import.import_items loads ALL existing codes into memory (set comprehension over db.items) on every call. Fine for small catalogs but will degrade with 100k+ items; swap to per-code lookup or indexed check if scale matters.
_num() parses '49.500' correctly only when the thousand pattern matches `\d{1,3}(\.\d{3})+`; '49.500,25' also works. But a plain '49.5' is correctly left as 49.5. OK.

Error message for unknown ValueError from float conversion in _clean/_num is translated to '<label> bukan angka' only when ValueError is raised; however _num itself raises ValueError via float() on bad strings — path is covered. Good.
Dry run performs the exact same validation + duplicate detection as the real run but doesn't persist; semantics are identical which is exactly what the UI needs. Good.
ImportItemsDialog uses `onDone()` after submit; parent Barang.jsx likely re-fetches items. Confirmed working in UI test (new item appears after import).

File size check reads full body before testing length — a 50MB upload will still be fully buffered in memory before the 400 is returned. Low risk given 5MB cap on client side but consider streaming/early rejection via Content-Length header for robustness.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of smoke-tested flows (dialog open -> dry-run -> import -> toast -> list refresh -> template download)

seed_data_creation: Each pytest run adds a few TEST_-prefixed items (TEST_Oli_<ts>, TEST_Dup1_<ts>, TEST_Import_New_<ts>) and renames demo items 200000000001 and 200000000002 to TEST_Update_* / TEST_Import_Upd_*. One IMPORT-ref stock move is logged per real import. Previous demo names on 200000000001/02 are not restored.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature 19 is working end-to-end. Login flow: POST /api/auth/login then landing URL is '/' (NOT '/dashboard'); don't wait_for_url('**/dashboard**'). For UI xlsx upload use page.set_input_files on [data-testid=item-import-file] (openpyxl isn't available inside the browser-automation runtime, so build the xlsx in a prior bash step and reference the /tmp path). Expected testids in dialog: item-import-dialog, item-import-template-button, item-import-file, item-import-check-button, item-import-summary, item-import-count-{baru,update,error}, item-import-table, item-import-row-{n}, item-import-submit. Backend endpoint pair: GET /api/items/import-template (owner only, xlsx) and POST /api/items/import?dry_run=true|false (multipart 'file', owner only). Stock movements endpoint is /api/stock/moves?item_code=.... Regression suites in /app/backend/tests/ run in ~11s with pytest-xdist.
